questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, and showers do not speed up this process.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: It is not safe to pass here.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass here.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot legally pass another vehicle in that area. It is usually in places where you cannot see far ahead, making passing unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?
questions.explanation: When being passed, keep your speed steady and do not speed up. Let the other vehicle pass safely and merge back into your lane.

questions.question: What is the term for the amount of alcohol in the blood?
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means you are more impaired.

questions.question: When it is hard to see during dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, what should you turn on so others know you are there?
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever visibility is poor or when other drivers may have trouble seeing you. Use low beams when you need to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, even without a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always use your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This pentagon-shaped sign means you are near a school or school crossing. Stay alert and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: Which of these is against the law?

options.text: Passing in a marked no passing zone.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass in no passing zones, on hills, in curves, or anywhere you cannot see far ahead. You also cannot pass at railroad crossings, street crossings, or in work zones.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Brake as hard as you can.

questions.explanation: When your car skids, ease off the gas or brake to regain control. Steer in the direction the car is sliding.

questions.question: When is the maximum posted speed limit safe to drive?
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the maximum safe speed only when conditions are perfect. Always adjust your speed based on traffic, weather, and road conditions.

questions.question: What should drivers do if they are worried, nervous, or angry?

options.text: They will be more alert and focused.

questions.explanation: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or upset, let someone else drive. Your emotions distract you from driving safely.

questions.question: What is the only thing that removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol and its effects from your body.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. How can you prevent it in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Move to the road shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: In rain, reduce your speed to prevent hydroplaning. When you drive too fast, your tires can rise up on the water and lose contact with the road, making your car hard to control.

questions.question: What does safe interstate driving require?

options.text: The ability to safely drive at higher speeds

questions.explanation: Safe highway driving requires you to stay alert at all times and be able to drive safely at higher speeds.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down and adjust your braking to avoid accidents and brake damage.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark construction zones. Drive carefully and slowly.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers have trouble seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle easier to see. If you need to use your windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road will curve right, then curve left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder. This helps you make sure it is safe to change lanes.

questions.question: When a pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only have to yield at intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use guide dogs or carry white canes. You must always yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: You must obey a police officer's directions, even if they contradict traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You never need to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Complete your turn only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are generally:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a reverse curve. The road curves to the right, then curves to the left.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights, you should:

options.text: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop completely when an emergency vehicle displays flashing red or blue lights and sounds its siren. Do not try to outrun it.

questions.question: When approaching a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, you should:

options.text: Honk so they know to move.

questions.explanation: You must stop and yield the right-of-way to any blind person using a guide dog or carrying a white cane. Let them safely cross the intersection before you proceed.

questions.question: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, a driver should:

options.text: Have their exhaust system checked regularly for leaks.
Keep the engine off when parked in an enclosed garage.

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is odorless and deadly. Signs include sudden tiredness, yawning, dizziness, and nausea. The only cure is fresh air.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a rest stop to nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for rest.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is ready to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off your engine until they cross.
Tell them when to cross the street.
Wait until they cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until they cross the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes always have the right-of-way. Let them cross completely before you turn.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags:

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are important safety devices. For best protection, always wear both lap and shoulder belts with airbags.
